description.value: A systematic review of studies examining neuropsychological measures of general cognition and executive functions as predictors of therapeutic adherence and relapse in patients with substance use disorders.

spans.text: This systematic review aims to examine growing evidence linking cognitive-executive functions with addiction treatment outcomes, and to discuss significant cognitive predictors drawing upon addiction neuroscience theory.

description.value: The review included empirical studies of patients undergoing outpatient or residential treatment for substance use disorders, assessed with neuropsychological measures before treatment or at treatment commencement, and reporting treatment adherence or relapse outcomes.

spans.text: The criteria for selection of articles were: 1) Participants in the study were undergoing treatment for substance use disorders (outpatient or residential), 2) Participants were assessed with neuropsychological measures of executive functions before onset or at treatment commencement, 3) The study included at least a measure of treatment outcome related to adherence/dropout during treatment, or with abstinence/relapse after treatment.
The sample size of studies for predicting treatment adherence ( M = 77.22; SD = 45.46) was larger than those for predicting relapse ( M = 53.47; SD = 38.22).
